'''Takuzo Aida''' (相田 卓三, ''Aida Takuzō'', born 3 May 1956) is a Japanese polymer chemist specializing in supramolecular chemistry and materials science. He is deputy director of the RIKEN Center for Emergent Matter Science and a distinguished professor in the Department of Chemistry and Biotechnology at the University of Tokyo.

== Early life and education ==
Aida was born in Ōita Prefecture, Japan.<ref name="aidacreativehub">{{cite web |title=Takuzo AIDA |url=https://www.aidacreativehub.com/takuzo-aida |website=Aida Creative Hub |access-date=2025-11-24 |archive-date=2025-11-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251124000000/https://www.aidacreativehub.com/takuzo-aida}}</ref> He earned a [[Bachelor of Engineering]] in physical chemistry from [[Yokohama National University]] in 1979. He then pursued graduate studies in polymer chemistry at the University of Tokyo under Shohei Inoue, receiving a Master of Engineering in 1981 and a Doctor of Engineering in 1984.<ref name="riken">{{cite web |title=Emergent Soft Matter Function Research Group |url=https://cems.riken.jp/en/laboratory/esmfrg |website=RIKEN Center for Emergent Matter Science |access-date=2025-11-24 |archive-date=2025-11-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251124000000/https://cems.riken.jp/en/laboratory/esmfrg}}</ref>

== Career ==
Following his doctorate, Aida joined the University of Tokyo as a research assistant in 1984, advancing to lecturer in 1989 and associate professor in 1991. He was appointed full professor in the Department of Chemistry and Biotechnology in 1996.<ref name="aidacreativehub" /> In 2008, he began a concurrent appointment at RIKEN, where he served as director of the RIKEN Advanced Science Institute until 2012 and has been deputy director of the Center for Emergent Matter Science since 2013.<ref name="riken" /> In 2022, the University of Tokyo designated him a distinguished professor.<ref>{{cite web |title=Distinguished University Professor Takuzo Aida was elected as an international member of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences |url=https://www.t.u-tokyo.ac.jp/en/topics/tp2023-06-12-001 |website=University of Tokyo |date=2023-06-12 |access-date=2025-11-24 |archive-date=2025-11-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251124000000/https://www.t.u-tokyo.ac.jp/en/topics/tp2023-06-12-001}}</ref>

Aida has served on the Board of Reviewing Editors for ''[[Science (journal)|Science]]'' since 2009 and on the advisory board of the ''[[Journal of the American Chemical Society]]'' from 2014 to 2021.<ref name="aidacreativehub" />

He was elected a foreign member of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2020,<ref>{{Cite web |title=UTokyo professor joins Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences |url=https://www.u-tokyo.ac.jp/focus/en/articles/z0508_00111.html |access-date=2025-11-24 |website=The University of Tokyo |language=en}}</ref> a member of the [[National Academy of Engineering]] in 2021,<ref>{{cite web |title=Dr. Takuzo Aida |url=https://www.nae.edu/250164/Dr-Takuzo-Aida |website=National Academy of Engineering |access-date=2025-11-24 |archive-date=2025-11-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251124000000/https://www.nae.edu/250164/Dr-Takuzo-Aida}}</ref> and an international honorary member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2023.<ref>{{cite web |title=Takuzo Aida |url=https://www.amacad.org/person/takuzo-aida |website=American Academy of Arts and Sciences |date=14 September 2025 |access-date=2025-11-24 |archive-date=2025-11-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251124000000/https://www.amacad.org/person/takuzo-aida}}</ref>

== Research ==
Aida's research focuses on supramolecular polymers, including self-assembly, controlled polymerization, and applications in functional materials such as conductive nanotubes and self-healing polymers.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Sim |first1=Seunghyun |last2=Hosono |first2=Nobuhiko |last3=Wei |first3=Zhang |last4=Jiang |first4=Donglin |last5=Yamamoto |first5=Yohei |date=2023 |title=Professor Takuzo Aida – A visionary leader in polymer science |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/pol.20230221 |journal=Journal of Polymer Science |volume=61 |issue=10 |pages=859–860 |doi=10.1002/pol.20230221 |issn=2642-4169}}</ref> Key contributions include:

* Development of "immortal polymerization," a [[living polymerization]] technique tolerant to [[chain transfer]] (1988).<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Aida |first1=Takuzo |last2=Takemura |first2=Akihiko |last3=Fuse |first3=Masahiro |last4=Inoue |first4=Shohei |date=1988 |title=Synthesis of a novel amphiphilic porphyrin carrying water-soluble polyether side chains of controlled chain length. Formation of a cofacial molecular assembly in aqueous media |url=https://pubs.rsc.org/en/content/articlelanding/1988/c3/c39880000391 |journal=Journal of the Chemical Society, Chemical Communications |issue=5 |pages=391–393 |doi=10.1039/C39880000391 |issn=0022-4936|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
* Self-assembled graphitic nanotubes from hexabenzocoronene derivatives, enabling electronic conductivity and helical chirality (2004–2011).<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Hill |first1=Jonathan P. |last2=Jin |first2=Wusong |last3=Kosaka |first3=Atsuko |last4=Fukushima |first4=Takanori |last5=Ichihara |first5=Hideki |last6=Shimomura |first6=Takeshi |last7=Ito |first7=Kohzo |last8=Hashizume |first8=Tomihiro |last9=Ishii |first9=Noriyuki |last10=Aida |first10=Takuzo |date=2004 |title=Self-Assembled, Hexa-peri-hexabenzocoronene Graphitic Nanotube |url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.1097789 |journal=Science |volume=304 |issue=5676 |pages=1481–1483 |doi=10.1126/science.1097789 |pmid=15178796 |bibcode=2004Sci...304.1481H |issn=0036-8075|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
* Chain-growth supramolecular polymerization, distinct from traditional step-growth mechanisms (2015).<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Kang |first1=Jiheong |last2=Miyajima |first2=Daigo |last3=Mori |first3=Tadashi |last4=Inoue |first4=Yoshihisa |last5=Itoh |first5=Yoshimitsu |last6=Aida |first6=Takuzo |date=2015 |title=A rational strategy for the realization of chain-growth supramolecular polymerization |url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.aaa4249 |journal=Science |volume=347 |issue=6222 |pages=646–651 |doi=10.1126/science.aaa4249 |pmid=25657246 |bibcode=2015Sci...347..646K |issn=0036-8075|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
* Thermally bisignate supramolecular polymerization, yielding distinct structures upon heating or cooling (2017).<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Venkata Rao |first1=Kotagiri |last2=Miyajima |first2=Daigo |last3=Nihonyanagi |first3=Atsuko |last4=Aida |first4=Takuzo |date=2017 |title=Thermally bisignate supramolecular polymerization |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/nchem.2812 |journal=Nature Chemistry |volume=9 |issue=11 |pages=1133–1139 |doi=10.1038/nchem.2812 |pmid=29064499 |bibcode=2017NatCh...9.1133V |issn=1755-4349|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
* Mechanically robust, self-repairable poly(ether thiourea) via noncovalent cross-linking (2018).<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Yanagisawa |first1=Yu |last2=Nan |first2=Yiling |last3=Okuro |first3=Kou |last4=Aida |first4=Takuzo |date=2018 |title=Mechanically robust, readily repairable polymers via tailored noncovalent cross-linking |url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.aam7588 |journal=Science |volume=359 |issue=6371 |pages=72–76 |doi=10.1126/science.aam7588 |pmid=29242235 |bibcode=2018Sci...359...72Y |issn=0036-8075|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
* Solvent-free autocatalytic supramolecular polymerization of phthalocyanines (2021).<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Chen |first1=Zhen |last2=Suzuki |first2=Yukinaga |last3=Imayoshi |first3=Ayumi |last4=Ji |first4=Xiaofan |last5=Rao |first5=Kotagiri Venkata |last6=Omata |first6=Yuki |last7=Miyajima |first7=Daigo |last8=Sato |first8=Emiko |last9=Nihonyanagi |first9=Atsuko |last10=Aida |first10=Takuzo |date=2021 |title=Solvent-free autocatalytic supramolecular polymerization |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/s41563-021-01122-z |journal=Nature Materials |volume=21 |issue=2 |pages=253–261 |doi=10.1038/s41563-021-01122-z |pmid=34650229 |issn=1476-4660|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

His work also encompasses photoenergy harvesting in dendrimers and redox-responsive nanostructures.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Jiang |first1=Dong-Lin |last2=Aida |first2=Takuzo |date=1997 |title=Photoisomerization in dendrimers by harvesting of low-energy photons |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/41290 |journal=Nature |volume=388 |issue=6641 |pages=454–456 |doi=10.1038/41290 |bibcode=1997Natur.388..454J |issn=|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
Aida's contributions have been recognized with numerous awards, including:
* 1993: Society of Polymer Science, Japan Award<ref name="aidacreativehub" />
* 2005: Inoue Prize for Science<ref name="chemistryviews2021">{{cite web |title=3rd Ryoji Noyori ACES Award |url=https://www.chemistryviews.org/3rd-ryoji-noyori-aces-award/ |website=ChemistryViews |date=2021-10-20 |access-date=2025-11-24 |archive-date=2025-11-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251124000000/https://www.chemistryviews.org/3rd-ryoji-noyori-aces-award/}}</ref>
* 2008: [[Chemical Society of Japan]] Award<ref name="chemistryviews2021" />
* 2009: [[American Chemical Society|ACS Award in Polymer Chemistry]]<ref>{{cite web |title=ACS Award in Polymer Chemistry Recipients |url=https://www.acs.org/content/acs/en/funding-and-awards/awards/acs-award-in-polymer-chemistry/past-recipients.html |website=American Chemical Society |access-date=2025-11-24 |archive-date=2025-11-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251124000000/https://www.acs.org/content/acs/en/funding-and-awards/awards/acs-award-in-polymer-chemistry/past-recipients.html}}</ref>
* 2010: Medal of Honor with Purple Ribbon<ref>{{cite web |title=Medal of Honor with Purple Ribbon awarded to Takuzo Aida |url=https://www.riken.jp/en/news_pubs/news/2010/20101104/index.html |website=RIKEN |date=2010-11-04 |access-date=2025-11-24 |archive-date=2025-11-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251124000000/https://www.riken.jp/en/news_pubs/news/2010/20101104/index.html}}</ref>
* 2011: [[Humboldt Research Award]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Prof. Dr. Takuzo Aida - Profile |url=https://www.humboldt-foundation.de/en/search-the-database/profil-1141251?set_language=en |website=Alexander von Humboldt Foundation |access-date=2025-11-24 |archive-date=2025-11-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251124000000/https://www.humboldt-foundation.de/en/search-the-database/profil-1141251?set_language=en}}</ref>
* 2015: [[Leo Esaki]] Prize<ref name="chemistryviews2021" />
* 2017: [[Chirality Medal]]<ref name="aidacreativehub" />
* 2018: [[Imperial Prize of the Japan Academy|Japan Academy Prize]]<ref>{{cite web |title=The Imperial Prize, Japan Academy Prize, Duke of Edinburgh Prize Recipients |url=https://www.japan-acad.go.jp/en/prizes/2018/031201.html |website=The Japan Academy |date=2018-03-12 |access-date=2025-11-24 |archive-date=2025-11-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251124000000/https://www.japan-acad.go.jp/en/prizes/2018/031201.html}}</ref>
* 2021: Ryoji Noyori ACES Award<ref name="chemistryviews2021" />
* 2021: Netherlands Award for Supramolecular Chemistry<ref>{{cite web |title=Professor Takuzo Aida received 2021 The Netherlands Award for Supramolecular Chemistry |url=https://www.t.u-tokyo.ac.jp/en/topics/foee/topics/setnws_202107121913277677277862.html |website=University of Tokyo |date=2021-07-12 |access-date=2025-11-24 |archive-date=2025-11-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251124000000/https://www.t.u-tokyo.ac.jp/en/topics/foee/topics/setnws_202107121913277677277862.html}}</ref>
